knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gu_2023_buprenorphine"))$reference`
* Buprenorphine model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gu_2023_buprenorphine"))$description`
* Naloxone model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gu_2023_naloxone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2023.1089862> (open access)
* Supplement: <https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2023.1089862/full#supplementary-material>
  (Tables S1-S3 and the NONMEM control streams of both final models)

Gu et al. analysed buprenorphine (BUP), its metabolite norbuprenorphine
(norBUP) and naloxone (NLX) after the sublingual buprenorphine/naloxone 4:1
tablet. Because the two drugs do not interact pharmacokinetically, the authors
fitted two separate NONMEM models, and they are packaged here as two files:

* `Gu_2023_buprenorphine` -- a parent-metabolite model. Buprenorphine has
  two-compartment disposition and Savic transit absorption (8 transit
  compartments, fixed) into an absorption compartment emptied at first order.
  Its relative bioavailability falls by 3.5% per swallow after dosing (centred on
  3 swallows). Norbuprenorphine (two compartments) is formed from the whole
  buprenorphine clearance, with the fraction metabolised fixed to 1 at 4 and
  8 mg and multiplied by 1.98 at 16 mg.
* `Gu_2023_naloxone` -- a one-compartment model with first-order absorption, a
  fixed sublingual bioavailability of 0.01 at the 8 mg dose level and a power
  effect of dose on that bioavailability.

**Dosing.** Both models take the dose in **mg of labelled buprenorphine** (one
tablet = 2 mg buprenorphine + 0.5 mg naloxone). In `Gu_2023_buprenorphine` the
dose goes to `transit1`, the first compartment of the transit chain; in
`Gu_2023_naloxone` it goes to `depot`, and its `amt` is *not* the naloxone
content: an 8 mg buprenorphine dose carrying 2 mg naloxone is entered as
`amt = 8`, exactly as in the source data (see *Assumptions and deviations*).
Both models also need the covariate `DOSE_BPN_SL_MG` set to the same per-dose
value; the buprenorphine model also needs `NSWALLOWS`, the number of swallows
after the dose. Concentrations are
returned in ng/mL (the paper reports ng/L).

# Population

46 Han Chinese men took part at Beijing Anding Hospital (Table 1): 34 healthy
volunteers received a single dose of 4 mg (n = 12), 8 mg (n = 12) or 16 mg
(n = 10) buprenorphine under naltrexone blockade, and 12 patients with opioid
use disorder (OUD) took 8 mg once daily for 8 days. Median age was 27.5 years
(20-44) and median weight 65.0 kg (53-88). The number of swallows after the
dose was recorded only in the single-dose groups: median 3.5 (0-8) at 4 mg, 2
(0-3) at 8 mg and 6.5 (2-12) at 16 mg; it was imputed with 2 in the multiple-dose
group. The data comprised 699 buprenorphine, 691 norbuprenorphine and 484
naloxone concentrations. Below-LLOQ data were under 10% for buprenorphine and
norbuprenorphine (discarded) and 20.3% / 56.2% (single / multiple dose) for
naloxone (M3 method).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Gu_2023_buprenorphine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
supplementary control streams were used to confirm structure, and they settle
two points the printed tables leave ambiguous (see *Assumptions and
deviations*).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (BUP CL/F) | 270 L/h | Table 4 |
| `lvc` (BUP Vc/F) | 377 L | Table 4 |
| `lvp` (BUP Vp/F) | 5879 L | Table 4 |
| `lq` (BUP Q/F) | 404 L/h | Table 4 |
| `lka` | 0.397 1/h | Table 4 |
| `lmtt` | 0.234 h | Table 4 |
| `lntr` | 8 (fixed) | Control stream THETA(6) `(8) FIX`; Figure 1A |
| `e_nswallows_fdepot` | -0.035 | Table 4 'The effect of NOS on F'; control stream `TVSLDO=DOSE*(1+THETA(8)*(NOS-3))` |
| `fm` | 1 (fixed) | Section 3.1.1; control stream THETA(17) `(1) FIX` |
| `e_dose16_fm` | 1.98 | Table 4 'Fm increment of 16 mg'; control stream `IF(DOSE.EQ.16) FFACTOR = THETA(18)` |
| `lcl_norbup` | 264 L/h | Control stream `TVCLM=THETA(10)` (Table 4 row labelled 'V C norBUP /Fm') |
| `lvc_norbup` | 22.2 L | Control stream `TVV4=THETA(9)` (Table 4 row labelled 'CL norBUP /Fm') |
| `lvp_norbup` | 5170 L | Table 4 |
| `lq_norbup` | 705 L/h | Table 4 |
| BUP IIV (CL, Vc, Vp, Q, MTT) | 33.2, 135.6, 41.4, 49.4, 37.5 %CV | Table 4; `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2` (control stream `$OMEGA`) |
| norBUP IIV (CL, Vc, Vp, Q) | 50.5, 119.6, 45.1, 56.7 %CV | Table 4 (CL / Vc rows swapped, as above) |
| `propSd`, `propSd_norbup` | 0.281, 0.22 | Table 4; additive parts `(0) FIX` in the control stream |
| NLX `lcl`, `lvc`, `lka` | 205 L/h, 104 L, 0.585 1/h | Table 3 |
| NLX `lfdepot` | 0.01 (fixed) | Table 3; control stream THETA(4) `0.01 FIX` |
| NLX `e_dose_fdepot` | -0.36 | Table 3; control stream `TVF1 = THETA(4)*(DOSE/8)**THETA(7)` |
| NLX IIV (CL, Vc) | 31.2, 102.5 %CV | Table 3 |
| NLX `propSd`, `addSd` | 0.208, 9.24 ng/L | Table 3; control stream `SD = SQRT(THETA(5)**2*IPRED**2 + THETA(6)**2)` |
| Savic transit input | n/a | Control stream `$DES` `DADT(1)`, with `LNFAC = LOG(2.5066)+(N+0.5)*LOG(N)-N`; explicit 9-compartment chain here |
| Parent-metabolite ODEs | n/a | Control stream `$DES` `DADT(2)`-`DADT(5)` |
| Concentration scaling | n/a | Control streams `CP = A(2)/V2*1000000`, `S2=V/1000000` (ng/L; ng/mL here) |

# Mass-balance and covariate checks (typical values)

These deterministic checks confirm that the transit chain delivers the dose,
that the metabolite is formed from the whole parent clearance, and
that the covariate effects have the published size. Each one goes red on a
zeroed or doubled input, a wrong clearance or a mis-signed covariate.

```{r helpers}
# Event table for the parent-metabolite model. Doses go to `transit1`, the
# first compartment of the explicit transit chain. With two declared error
# endpoints every observation row nominates one via `dvid`; both Cc and
# Cc_norbup come back as columns. Covariates follow the event columns.
bup_events <- function(ids, dose_times, dose_amt, obs_times, nswallows) {
  dose_amt <- rep_len(dose_amt, length(dose_times))
  one <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = dose_amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "transit1", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  # DOSE_BPN_SL_MG is the most recent dose (only the 16 mg level changes the
  # norbuprenorphine Fm; buprenorphine itself does not depend on it).
  one$DOSE_BPN_SL_MG <- dose_amt[findInterval(one$time, dose_times)]
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(i) dplyr::mutate(one, id = i)))
  ev$NSWALLOWS <- rep_len(nswallows, length(ids))[match(ev$id, ids)]
  dplyr::select(ev, id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dvid, DOSE_BPN_SL_MG, NSWALLOWS)
}

# Event table for the one-endpoint naloxone model: observations on `central`.
nlx_events <- function(ids, dose_times, dose_amt, obs_times) {
  dose_amt <- rep_len(dose_amt, length(dose_times))
  one <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, amt = dose_amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  one$DOSE_BPN_SL_MG <- dose_amt[findInterval(one$time, dose_times)]
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(i) dplyr::mutate(one, id = i)))
  dplyr::select(ev, id, time, amt, evid, cmt, DOSE_BPN_SL_MG)
}

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
```

```{r mass-balance}
mod_bup <- readModelDb("Gu_2023_buprenorphine")
mod_nlx <- readModelDb("Gu_2023_naloxone")
bup_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_bup)
nlx_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_nlx)

# Log-spaced grid to 2000 h: the norbuprenorphine terminal phase is long.
grid <- c(0, 10^seq(-3, log10(2000), length.out = 4000))
# Stirling's approximation to log(8!) in the control stream makes the transit
# input deliver 1.0105 times the bioavailable dose.
stirling <- exp(lgamma(9) - (log(2.5066) + 8.5 * log(8) - 8))

mb <- lapply(c(4, 8, 16), function(d) {
  lapply(c(3, 4), function(nos) {
    ev <- bup_events(1L, 0, d, grid, nos)
    s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(bup_typ, ev, atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10))
    s <- s[!duplicated(s$time), ]
    data.frame(
      dose = d, nos = nos,
      bup_ratio = 270 * trap(s$time, s$Cc) / 1000 / d,
      norbup_ratio = 264 * trap(s$time, s$Cc_norbup) / 1000 / d
    )
  }) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

mb <- mb |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f_expected = (1 - 0.035 * (nos - 3)) * stirling,
    fm_expected = ifelse(dose == 16, 1.98, 1)
  )
knitr::kable(mb, digits = 5,
  caption = "CL x AUC(0-inf) / dose for buprenorphine and norbuprenorphine (typical values).")

stopifnot(
  # CL/F x AUC = F(NOS) x dose x Stirling factor.
  all(abs(mb$bup_ratio / mb$f_expected - 1) < 1e-3),
  # CLm/Fm x AUCm = Fm x F(NOS) x dose x Stirling factor.
  all(abs(mb$norbup_ratio / (mb$f_expected * mb$fm_expected) - 1) < 1e-3)
)

nlx_mb <- lapply(c(4, 8, 16), function(d) {
  ev <- nlx_events(1L, 0, d, grid[grid <= 400])
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(nlx_typ, ev, atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10))
  s <- s[!duplicated(s$time), ]
  data.frame(dose = d, ratio = 205 * trap(s$time, s$Cc) / 1000 / d,
             f_expected = 0.01 * (d / 8)^-0.36)
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
knitr::kable(nlx_mb, digits = 5,
  caption = "Naloxone CL x AUC(0-inf) / dose against F = 0.01 (DOSE/8)^-0.36.")
stopifnot(all(abs(nlx_mb$ratio / nlx_mb$f_expected - 1) < 1e-3))
```

The 3.5% fall in buprenorphine bioavailability per additional swallow (Abstract
and Section 4.3) is the `nos = 4` versus `nos = 3` rows above, and the 1.98-fold
higher norbuprenorphine exposure per unit of parent clearance at 16 mg
(Section 4.3) is the 16 mg `norbup_ratio`.

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. Each published dose group is simulated with
200 virtual subjects at the paper's sampling times (Section 2.4). The number of
swallows is set to the Table 1 median of each single-dose group, and to 2 in
the multiple-dose group, as the authors imputed it.

```{r cohort}
n_arm <- 200L
sd_times <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72)
md_doses <- seq(0, 168, by = 24)
md_times <- c(0, 120, 144, 168 + c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24))

arms <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("4 mg", "8 mg", "16 mg", "8 mg QD x 8 d"),
  dose = c(4, 8, 16, 8),
  nos = c(3.5, 2, 6.5, 2),
  multiple = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

build_arm <- function(k, builder) {
  a <- arms[k, ]
  ids <- (k - 1L) * n_arm + seq_len(n_arm)
  dt <- if (a$multiple) md_doses else 0
  ot <- if (a$multiple) md_times else sd_times
  ev <- if (identical(builder, "bup")) {
    bup_events(ids, dt, a$dose, ot, a$nos)
  } else {
    nlx_events(ids, dt, a$dose, ot)
  }
  dplyr::mutate(ev, treatment = a$treatment)
}

ev_bup <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), build_arm, builder = "bup"))
ev_nlx <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), build_arm, builder = "nlx"))
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(unique(ev_bup[, c("id", "time", "evid")])),
  length(unique(ev_bup$id)) == 4L * n_arm
)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230119)
sim_bup <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_bup, events = ev_bup, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_nlx <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_nlx, events = ev_nlx, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

# The published predictive check summarises simulated observations, so the
# residual error of each model is added here (Tables 3 and 4) and values below
# the assay LLOQ (50 ng/L for BUP and norBUP, 20 ng/L for NLX; Section 2.5)
# are set to zero, which PKNCA treats as below the limit of quantification.
# Cc keeps this observation-scale value; ipred is the noise-free prediction.
set.seed(20230119)
add_ruv <- function(ipred, prop, add = 0, lloq) {
  obs <- ipred + sqrt((prop * ipred)^2 + add^2) * stats::rnorm(length(ipred))
  ifelse(obs < lloq, 0, obs)
}
sim_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_bup |> dplyr::transmute(id, time, treatment, analyte = "BUP", ipred = Cc,
                              Cc = add_ruv(Cc, 0.281, lloq = 0.05)),
  sim_bup |> dplyr::transmute(id, time, treatment, analyte = "norBUP", ipred = Cc_norbup,
                              Cc = add_ruv(Cc_norbup, 0.22, lloq = 0.05)),
  sim_nlx |> dplyr::transmute(id, time, treatment, analyte = "NLX", ipred = Cc,
                              Cc = add_ruv(Cc, 0.208, 0.00924, lloq = 0.02))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = arms$treatment),
    analyte = factor(analyte, levels = c("BUP", "norBUP", "NLX"))
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_long$Cc))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-2-3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates the single-dose panels of Figures 2 (buprenorphine and
# norbuprenorphine) and 3 (naloxone): median and 90% prediction interval of
# the noise-free predictions (the observation-scale values carry zeros for
# below-LLOQ samples, which a log axis cannot show).
sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "8 mg QD x 8 d", time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(ipred, 0.05), Q50 = median(ipred), Q95 = quantile(ipred, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
       colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
       caption = "Replicates the single-dose panels of Figures 2 and 3 of Gu 2023.")
```

```{r figure-2-md, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates the multiple-dose panels of Figures 2 and 3: day 8 of 8 mg QD.
sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "8 mg QD x 8 d", time >= 168) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(ipred, 0.05), Q50 = median(ipred), Q95 = quantile(ipred, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 168, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after the 8th dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Replicates the multiple-dose panels of Figures 2 and 3 of Gu 2023.")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper's numerical predictive check (Table S2) reports the median AUC and
Cmax of 1000 simulated replicates of each dose group: AUC0-72 h after a single
dose, and AUC over the 24 h after the eighth dose in the multiple-dose group.
Those medians are the reference here, because they are what the published model
itself predicts for these cohorts. Like the paper's check, the comparison uses
simulated observations: residual error is added and values below the assay
LLOQ are treated as unquantifiable.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment, analyte)
# Guarantee a pre-dose time-zero record per subject and analyte.
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, analyte) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, analyte, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(analyte, id, time)

nca_dose <- ev_bup |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + analyte + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = arms$treatment,
  start = ifelse(arms$multiple, 168, 0),
  end = ifelse(arms$multiple, 192, 72),
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against the published predictive check

```{r nca-compare}
# Table S2 'NPC result median', converted from ng/L and ng.h/L to ng/mL and
# ng.h/mL. The 8 mg buprenorphine AUC is printed '2768[23264-32262]'; its
# confidence interval shows a dropped digit, so 27680 is used.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~treatment, ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "BUP", "4 mg", 13103, 1643,
  "BUP", "8 mg", 27680, 3510,
  "BUP", "16 mg", 45388, 5795,
  "BUP", "8 mg QD x 8 d", 31222, 4108,
  "norBUP", "4 mg", 10949, 479,
  "norBUP", "8 mg", 23826, 1041,
  "norBUP", "16 mg", 77032, 3400,
  "norBUP", "8 mg QD x 8 d", 30246, 2187,
  "NLX", "4 mg", 244, 97,
  "NLX", "8 mg", 379, 147,
  "NLX", "16 mg", 590, 228,
  "NLX", "8 mg QD x 8 d", 420, 142
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auclast = auclast / 1000, cmax = cmax / 1000)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = c("analyte", "treatment"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp,
  caption = "Simulated median NCA vs. the Table S2 predictive-check medians. * differs by >20%.")

pct <- as.numeric(sub("%[*]?$", "", cmp[["% diff"]]))
stopifnot(
  length(pct) == 24L, !anyNA(pct),
  # A mis-transcribed clearance, volume or covariate moves these medians by
  # tens of percent; the medians of 200 subjects sit within a few percent.
  # Realised: median -3%, 90th percentile of |% diff| 7.1%.
  abs(median(pct)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(pct), 0.9) < 20
)
```

Buprenorphine and norbuprenorphine Cmax and AUC, and the single-dose naloxone
values, agree with the published medians to within about 10%. The exception is
the naloxone AUC after the eighth dose (about 25% low). In that group 56% of
the observed naloxone samples were below the LLOQ (Section 4.1), so the
simulated AUC depends heavily on how below-LLOQ values are counted, which the
paper does not state for its predictive check; here they count as zero. Without
the LLOQ step, the single-dose naloxone AUCs are instead inflated by additive
noise in the 72 h tail. The model also reproduces the two dose-dependent
features the paper set out to explain: the less than dose-proportional
buprenorphine exposure at 16 mg (more swallows, lower bioavailability) and the
more than dose-proportional norbuprenorphine exposure
at 16 mg (higher Fm).

# Dose optimisation (Figures 4-6)

The authors simulated six regimens to steady state and evaluated day 8. The
buprenorphine concentration is converted to mu-opioid receptor occupancy with
the Emax model of Nasser et al. (2014) quoted in Section 3.5.2
(Emax 91.4%, EC50 0.67 ng/mL). The dosing clock times and the number of swallows
used for these simulations are not reported; doses are spaced evenly through the
day and every subject swallows twice (the 8 mg median).

```{r regimens}
regimens <- list(
  "16 mg QD" = list(times = 0, amt = 16),
  "8 mg BID" = list(times = c(0, 12), amt = 8),
  "16 mg + 8 mg" = list(times = c(0, 12), amt = c(16, 8)),
  "8 mg TID" = list(times = c(0, 8, 16), amt = 8),
  "16 mg BID" = list(times = c(0, 12), amt = 16),
  "16 mg + 8 mg + 8 mg" = list(times = c(0, 8, 16), amt = c(16, 8, 8))
)
day8 <- seq(168, 192, by = 0.25)

build_regimen <- function(k, builder) {
  r <- regimens[[k]]
  ids <- (k - 1L) * n_arm + seq_len(n_arm)
  dt <- as.vector(outer(r$times, 24 * 0:7, "+"))
  da <- rep(r$amt, length.out = length(r$times))[rep(seq_along(r$times), 8)]
  ev <- if (identical(builder, "bup")) {
    bup_events(ids, dt, da, c(0, day8), 2)
  } else {
    nlx_events(ids, dt, da, c(0, day8))
  }
  dplyr::mutate(ev, regimen = names(regimens)[k])
}
ev_reg_bup <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), build_regimen, builder = "bup"))
ev_reg_nlx <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), build_regimen, builder = "nlx"))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20230120)
reg_bup <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_bup, events = ev_reg_bup, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 168) |>
  dplyr::mutate(oro = 91.4 * Cc / (0.67 + Cc),
                regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens)))
reg_nlx <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_nlx, events = ev_reg_nlx, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 168) |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = names(regimens)))
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 4: probability of reaching each %T > MSC (3 ng/mL) target
# on day 8.
tmsc <- reg_bup |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct_t = 100 * mean(Cc >= 3), .groups = "drop")
pta <- tidyr::crossing(target = seq(0, 100, by = 10), tmsc) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, target) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(pct_t >= target), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pta, aes(target, pta, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "%T > MSC target (%)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = "Regimen",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Gu 2023.")
pta |>
  dplyr::filter(target == 50) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, pta) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "PTA at 50% T > MSC (%)" = pta) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)
```

For 8 mg TID the simulated probability of keeping buprenorphine above 3 ng/mL
for at least half of day 8 is close to the paper's ~70%. The two 16 mg BID and
16 + 8 + 8 mg regimens come out higher than the paper's ~70%, as expected from
giving every 16 mg dose the two-swallow bioavailability; the 16 mg group in the
trial swallowed a median 6.5 times.

```{r figure-5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 5: receptor occupancy on day 8, median and 90% PI.
oro_sum <- reg_bup |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(oro, 0.05), Q50 = median(oro),
                   Q95 = quantile(oro, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(oro_sum, aes(time - 168, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 70, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(x = "Time on day 8 (h)", y = "mu-opioid receptor occupancy (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Gu 2023.")
```

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 6: naloxone concentration on day 8, median and 90% PI,
# against the 4.6 ng/mL withdrawal threshold.
nlx_sum <- reg_nlx |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc),
                   Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(nlx_sum, aes(time - 168, Q50, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4.6, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time on day 8 (h)", y = "Naloxone (ng/mL)",
       colour = "Regimen", fill = "Regimen",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Gu 2023.")

nlx_cmax_tid <- reg_nlx |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "8 mg TID") |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
oro_tid <- oro_sum |> dplyr::filter(regimen == "8 mg TID")
stopifnot(
  # Section 4.5: with 8 mg TID the naloxone peak stays below 4.6 ng/mL in
  # more than 95% of patients (the simulated 95th percentile is far below).
  quantile(nlx_cmax_tid$cmax, 0.95) < 4.6,
  # Section 4.5: 8 mg TID achieves and maintains occupancy of at least 70%
  # (median over day 8). Realised minimum 73.5%; the standard error of a
  # 200-subject median occupancy is under 1 percentage point.
  min(oro_tid$Q50) > 70
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Norbuprenorphine CL and Vc.** Table 4 prints 22.2 against
  'CL norBUP /Fm, L/h' and 264 against 'V C norBUP /Fm, L', with the matching
  IIV rows (119.6% and 50.5%). The control stream assigns them the other way
  round (`TVV4=THETA(9)` with initial value 22.2, `TVCLM=THETA(10)` with 264;
  `$OMEGA` 1.43 on V4 and 0.255 on CLM). The control-stream reading is used:
  it reproduces the Table S2 norbuprenorphine medians (table above), whereas a
  clearance of 22.2 L/h would raise norbuprenorphine AUC about 12-fold.
* **Centring of the number of swallows.** The control stream centres on 3
  swallows (`NOS-3`), not on the Table 1 median of 2 that the general
  covariate equation of Section 3.3 would imply; the stream is used.
* **Transit absorption as an explicit chain.** The control stream writes the
  Savic transit input in closed form (`DADT(1)`), driven by the time since the
  dose, and removes the dose record's amount from the depot with `F1 = 0`. With
  the number of transit compartments fixed at the integer 8, a chain of 9
  compartments sharing the rate constant `ktr = 9 / MTT` delivers exactly the
  same input, and the dose is given to its first compartment. The chain is
  used because the closed-form input is zero at the dose and lasts only about
  0.2 h, so an ODE solver stepping between sparse observation times can pass
  over it entirely. Two consequences: the dose is entered on `transit1`, and a
  dose given while an earlier one is still in transit is superposed rather than
  restarting the input; with a mean transit time of 0.23 h this has no effect
  at any practical dosing interval.
* **Stirling factor in the transit input.** The control stream normalises the
  input with Stirling's approximation to log(n!), so at n = 8 it absorbs
  1.0105 times the bioavailable dose. The factor is reproduced on
  `f(transit1)`, and the mass-balance check above carries it explicitly.
* **Transit input driven by `amt`.** The control stream reads the dose for the
  transit input from its `DOSE` data column; the model uses the dose record's
  `amt`, so `amt` and `DOSE_BPN_SL_MG` carry the same value.
* **Naloxone dose units.** The naloxone model's bioavailability is a fixed
  0.01 at the 8 mg level (Table 3, citing McDonald et al. 2018), and the dose
  record carries the labelled buprenorphine strength, not the naloxone content:
  with `amt = 8` the model reproduces the Table S2 naloxone medians and the
  Discussion's dose-normalised AUC (39 ng.h/L per mg at 8 mg), whereas entering
  the 2 mg of naloxone would give exposures 4-fold too low. The maintainers
  kept the published parameterisation rather than re-expressing it per mg of
  naloxone with F = 0.04.
* **Units.** Doses are tablet labels (2 mg buprenorphine hydrochloride + 0.5 mg
  naloxone hydrochloride per tablet, Section 2.1); no salt correction is
  applied, as in the source. Norbuprenorphine is carried in buprenorphine-mass
  units (no molecular-weight conversion in the control stream).
* **Inter-individual variability.** Tables 3 and 4 print IIV as
  `sqrt(omega^2) * 100`; for example 135.6% for buprenorphine Vc is the square
  root of the control-stream estimate 1.84. Variances are therefore
  `(CV/100)^2`.
* **Naloxone structure.** Table S3 describes the final naloxone model as
  "two-compartment", but the main text (Sections 4.4 and 5) and the control
  stream (`ADVAN2 TRANS2`) use one compartment, which is what is packaged.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (age, weight, disease state for
  both drugs; number of swallows for naloxone) are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Simulation design for Figures 4-6.** Dosing clock times and the swallow
  counts behind the paper's "NOS-adjusted" doses are not reported; doses are
  spaced evenly and every virtual subject swallows twice. The PTA values above
  are therefore indicative only: the paper reports PTA near 70% at the 50%
  target for 8 mg TID, 16 mg BID and 16 + 8 + 8 mg. For norbuprenorphine, a
  16 mg dose in a mixed regimen switches Fm only while it is the most recent
  dose; this does not affect buprenorphine or the figures above.
* No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-10-15.
